claim_ceiling: Linear Fisher LDA ensemble of (1-Jaccard) and KS D FAILS to achieve TP>=0.8 and FP<=0.15 on drift-vs-noise discrimination in this bounded setting: aggregated per-condition mean Jaccard + KS D on synthetic CPU-bound mock server (computation ~9.3ms/field, R2=0.9999) with 4 schema sizes 10,20,30,50 x 6 patterns (add_field/remove_field/change_type drift vs optional_field_churn/null_valued_fields/nested_object_variation noise), N=24 conditions (16 train/8 test stratified, seed 20260916). AUC=0.625 (slightly above random), best operating point TP=0.5 FP=0.0 (threshold 0.4603), no point meets frozen rule. Positive control fails (TP 0.25 on train), weights inverted indicating noise more divergent than drift (2-field noise vs 1-field drift confound). Ceiling DOES NOT extend to: per-sample ROC (N=30 per condition), nonlinear ensembles (SVM/RF), other signal families (session tokens, field-usage profiling), real APIs (DB/cache/CDN), different noise magnitudes, or sizes outside 10-50. C-FRESHNESS remains HYPOTHESIS outside this linear two-signal setting.
unresolved: Whether nonlinear ensemble (SVM, random forest) on same two features could achieve TP>=0.8 FP<=0.15 despite linear failure — inverted direction suggests fundamental overlap, not just linear boundary
Whether per-sample data (N=30 actual Jaccard/KS per sample) instead of aggregated means would reveal different discrimination (audit recomputation limited to means)
Whether fresh_copy inclusion would change null_control FP and decision (fresh copies have Jaccard=1.0 KS~0.13-0.27, easily separable, but excluded from drift-vs-noise task)
Whether different noise magnitude (e.g., 1-2% churn vs 10%) or different mock server (real DB/cache) would undo inversion
Whether larger test (e.g., leave-one-size-out or N>=100 per condition with reduced jitter 0-10ms) would provide power to detect small temporal delta (~9ms vs 50ms jitter)
